phases.name: 1. Define the stream contract and core services
phases.description: Translate the frozen Kafka-like brief into producer, broker, coordination, processing, consumer, sink, and operational responsibilities.

phases.name: 2. Connect publishers, processors, and subscribers
phases.description: Wire every data and control path after its endpoint components exist so the walkthrough replays into one connected architecture.

phases.name: 3. Choose ordering, durability, and delivery semantics
phases.description: Make partition ordering, replicated commit, partition-failure, replay, delivery, and large-record tradeoffs explicit.

phases.name: 4. Scale from observed behavior and validate
phases.description: Scale from measured workload and lag, exercise recovery paths, and keep unspecified capacity and latency targets open.

steps.phase: 1. Define the stream contract and core services
steps.title: Frame the frozen streaming brief
steps.content: Design a distributed stream platform for publishing and subscribing to records, durable real-time processing, replay, graceful failure, and horizontal growth. The brief calls for millions of messages per second, order within a partition, low delivery latency, no data loss, records up to 1 MB, network-partition handling, and either exactly-once or at-least-once delivery. Its hints point to partitioning, replication, an append-only commit log, consumer groups, and ZooKeeper-like coordination. Treat the throughput phrase as a capability requirement, not a measured capacity target.

steps.phase: 1. Define the stream contract and core services
steps.title: Add producer applications
steps.content: Publishers assign a stable key to records whose order matters and a stable event ID for retry deduplication. They validate the brief's 1 MB maximum before sending and use broker acknowledgements to know when a record is committed.

component.label: Producer Applications
component.description: Applications that publish keyed records to named streams

properties.purpose: Publish records directly to the partition leader selected by the broker metadata. Include a stable event ID for safe retries, choose a stable partition key for records that require ordering, and reject payloads above the brief's 1 MB limit before transmission.

component.highlightReason: The producer establishes the identity, size, and ordering key that downstream retries and partition routing depend on.

steps.phase: 1. Define the stream contract and core services
steps.title: Add the partitioned broker and commit log
steps.content: The broker is the durable system of record for stream data. It appends records to ordered partition logs, replicates them across broker failure domains, tracks offsets, and serves independent consumer groups. Keep the partition count, replica placement, and replay retention policy tied to the workload and failure model; the brief does not set those values.

component.label: Partitioned Stream Broker
component.description: Replicated append-only log for named record streams

properties.purpose: Serve publish-subscribe streams from a partitioned append-only commit log. Preserve append order and offsets within each partition, replicate committed records across broker failure domains, store consumer-group offsets, and retain records for the replay window selected from product needs.

component.highlightReason: Durable partition logs and replicated commits provide the platform's storage, replay, and ordering boundary.

steps.phase: 1. Define the stream contract and core services
steps.title: Add cluster coordination
steps.content: Use a ZooKeeper-compatible coordination service for broker membership, controller election, partition-leader metadata, and fencing stale leaders. It belongs on the control plane; record payloads stay on the broker data plane. A consensus-backed metadata quorum is the alternative if operating an external coordinator is undesirable.

component.label: Cluster Coordination Service
component.description: Membership, controller election, and fenced partition leadership

properties.purpose: Coordinate broker membership and controller election, publish partition-leader metadata, and fence stale leaders after a network partition. The ZooKeeper backend represents the brief's coordination hint; this control plane never carries stream records.

component.highlightReason: A single current leader per partition prevents split-brain writes while the coordination quorum is healthy.

steps.phase: 1. Define the stream contract and core services
steps.title: Add real-time stream processing
steps.content: Processors consume partition records continuously, preserve each partition's order, checkpoint progress with state, and publish derived records when needed. Processing throughput is bounded by partition parallelism and the slowest stateful operation, so measure skew as well as aggregate rate.

component.label: Real-Time Processing Engine
component.description: Stateful and stateless operators over ordered stream partitions

properties.purpose: Continuously consume broker partitions for real-time filtering, transformation, joins, and stateful aggregation. Checkpoint operator state with committed input offsets, keep per-partition order, and publish derived streams through the broker.

component.highlightReason: This processing tier turns the durable log into real-time pipelines without making publishers wait for downstream work.

steps.phase: 1. Define the stream contract and core services
steps.title: Add consumer-group workers
steps.content: Each consumer group has its own offsets and can scale members across partitions. A group processes a partition in order; adding members beyond the group's assigned partition parallelism does not increase that group's useful concurrency.

component.label: Consumer Group Workers
component.description: Independent subscriber groups with partition assignments and offsets

properties.purpose: Run independent consumer groups that subscribe to named streams, divide assigned partitions among group members, and track a committed offset per partition. Reprocessing starts from an earlier retained offset; independent groups do not advance one another's cursors.

component.highlightReason: Consumer groups provide subscriber isolation, load balancing, and an explicit replay cursor.

steps.phase: 1. Define the stream contract and core services
steps.title: Add an example durable consumer sink
steps.content: The sink is an example downstream system, not a second source of truth for the stream. Make writes idempotent by event ID or use a transaction that commits output and input progress together when the sink supports it.

component.label: Consumer Output Store
component.description: Example durable destination for consumer results

properties.purpose: Persist application results written by a consumer group. Apply each stable event ID idempotently, or transact the result and consumer checkpoint together when supported; the broker log remains the replay source.

component.highlightReason: The sink boundary makes duplicate delivery and replay effects visible rather than assuming network-level exactly-once behavior.

steps.phase: 1. Define the stream contract and core services
steps.title: Add stream health monitoring
steps.content: Observe broker append latency, throughput, partition skew, under-replicated partitions, controller changes, consumer lag, retry volume, and processor checkpoint age. Alert on user-impacting symptoms using service objectives established from the actual workload.

component.label: Stream Health Monitoring
component.description: Metrics and alerts for data-plane and control-plane health

properties.purpose: Collect broker append and delivery latency, throughput, partition skew, replication health, coordinator elections, consumer lag, retry and dead-letter counts, and processor checkpoint age. Set alert thresholds from measured workload and agreed service objectives.

component.highlightReason: Lag, replication health, and partition skew reveal delivery and recovery problems before an aggregate throughput number does.

steps.phase: 1. Define the stream contract and core services
steps.title: Keep the control and data planes separate
steps.content: Publishers, processors, and consumer groups exchange records through the broker. Coordination changes membership and leadership metadata only. This boundary keeps record throughput from competing with controller operations and gives the commit log one clear durability authority.

steps.phase: 2. Connect publishers, processors, and subscribers
steps.title: Connect publishers to the broker
steps.content: Producer clients discover the current partition leader and publish records directly to it. The broker returns the configured commit acknowledgement; request size validation enforces the 1 MB record limit before append.

connection.label: Publish keyed records
connection.description: Send records to the selected partition leader, validate the 1 MB maximum, and return a commit acknowledgement under the chosen replication policy.

steps.phase: 2. Connect publishers, processors, and subscribers
steps.title: Connect coordination to broker leadership
steps.content: Broker controllers read membership and partition assignments from the coordinator. Leadership epochs fence a former leader after a partition so it cannot continue accepting writes with stale metadata.

connection.label: Membership and leader metadata
connection.description: Provide controller election, partition assignments, and fencing epochs on the control plane; record traffic remains on broker links.

steps.phase: 2. Connect publishers, processors, and subscribers
steps.title: Feed the real-time processing engine
steps.content: The processor consumes committed records by partition and checkpoints its state with input offsets. A slow operator creates lag in its assigned partitions, not a global ordering barrier.

connection.label: Consume committed partitions
connection.description: Stream ordered records and offsets to stateful or stateless operators for real-time processing.

steps.phase: 2. Connect publishers, processors, and subscribers
steps.title: Connect independent consumer groups
steps.content: Each subscription group receives partition assignments and advances only its own committed offsets. Group membership distributes partitions for parallel work while preserving order within each assigned partition.

connection.label: Subscribe by consumer group
connection.description: Deliver ordered partition records with independent group offsets for load balancing and replay.

steps.phase: 2. Connect publishers, processors, and subscribers
steps.title: Publish derived streams
steps.content: Derived events return to the broker as a new stream or topic. Use a stable output event ID and keep the processor's input checkpoint coordinated with its output commit where the runtime supports a transaction.

connection.label: Publish derived records
connection.description: Append transformed or aggregated events to a derived stream without bypassing broker durability and replay.

steps.phase: 2. Connect publishers, processors, and subscribers
steps.title: Persist consumer results
steps.content: Write the result before advancing the group's offset, or atomically commit the result and offset. If a crash occurs after the write but before the offset commit, replay may repeat the record, so the sink must deduplicate or make the operation idempotent.

connection.label: Apply idempotent consumer effects
connection.description: Persist each event safely before committing progress; replay after a partial failure must not duplicate the business effect.

steps.phase: 2. Connect publishers, processors, and subscribers
steps.title: Export broker health signals
steps.content: Expose per-partition append latency, leader and replica state, log utilization, produce errors, and coordinator changes to monitoring. Per-partition signals make hot partitions and replica loss visible even when cluster averages appear healthy.

connection.label: Broker and replica metrics
connection.description: Report append latency, throughput, partition skew, replication health, and controller transitions.

steps.phase: 2. Connect publishers, processors, and subscribers
steps.title: Export processing and lag signals
steps.content: Report consumer lag and processor checkpoint age by group and partition. These signals distinguish a broker delivery problem from a slow operator or sink.

connection.label: Consumer lag and checkpoint metrics
connection.description: Expose per-group lag, processing rate, retries, and checkpoint progress for scaling and recovery decisions.

steps.phase: 2. Connect publishers, processors, and subscribers
steps.title: Trace a record and its replay cursor
steps.content: A record is keyed and appended to one partition, replicated under the broker's commit policy, then read by each subscribed group at its own offset. A consumer can replay by moving that group's cursor to an earlier offset still present in the log; other groups continue unaffected.

steps.phase: 3. Choose ordering, durability, and delivery semantics
steps.title: Choose per-key ordering over a global sequence
steps.content: Hash a stable entity key to a partition and preserve append order there. This meets the brief's per-partition ordering guarantee while allowing separate partitions to progress in parallel.

decision.question: What ordering boundary should the stream guarantee?
decision.chosen: Stable-key order within a partition; no global total order across partitions
decision.chosenReason: The brief requires ordering within a partition. A stable key keeps related records together while partition-level parallelism supports horizontal scale.

alternatives.tradeoff: Simpler total-order reasoning, but a single serialization point limits parallel throughput and availability.
Can spread load, but related records may land in different partitions and lose their required order.

properties.purpose: Serve publish-subscribe streams from a partitioned append-only commit log. Route a stable entity key to one partition, preserve append order and offsets within that partition, replicate committed records across broker failure domains, store consumer-group offsets, and retain records for the replay window selected from product needs.

steps.phase: 3. Choose ordering, durability, and delivery semantics
steps.title: Acknowledge replicated commits
steps.content: Append at the partition leader and acknowledge only after the selected in-sync replica policy confirms the commit. This favors durability over the lowest possible acknowledgement latency; the exact replica count and acknowledgement policy depend on the deployment's failure domains and recovery objective.

decision.question: When should a producer receive a successful durable-write acknowledgement?
decision.chosen: After the configured in-sync replica commit policy is satisfied
decision.chosenReason: An acknowledgement before replication can report success for a record that disappears with its only copy. The policy must be chosen against the actual failure model.

alternatives.option: Acknowledge immediately after the leader append
alternatives.tradeoff: Reduces producer wait, but a leader failure before replication can lose an acknowledged record.
Can strengthen copy completion, but one unavailable replica can stall writes and increase latency.

properties.purpose: Serve publish-subscribe streams from a partitioned append-only commit log. Route a stable entity key to one partition and preserve order there. Replicate records across broker failure domains and acknowledge only after the selected in-sync replica commit policy is met. Store consumer-group offsets and retain records for the replay window selected from product needs.

steps.phase: 3. Choose ordering, durability, and delivery semantics
steps.title: Fence writes during a network partition
steps.content: Only the side with authoritative coordination quorum may elect leaders and advance metadata. Fence former leaders with epochs; replicas that cannot confirm the commit policy must stop acknowledging writes. This can reduce write availability on a minority side, which is the explicit tradeoff for avoiding split-brain commits and data loss.

decision.question: How should brokers behave when a network partition prevents agreement on leadership?
decision.chosen: Fence stale leaders and accept writes only through the authoritative leader under the commit policy
decision.chosenReason: Serving conflicting leaders risks divergent logs and acknowledged data loss. Fail closed for writes where leadership or the required replicas cannot be established, then reconcile from the committed log after quorum returns.

alternatives.option: Accept writes independently on both sides
alternatives.tradeoff: Preserves local write availability but creates conflicting histories that cannot preserve one partition order without conflict resolution.

alternatives.option: Keep the old leader active without fencing
alternatives.tradeoff: Can appear available during coordinator loss, but a recovered former leader may append after a newer leader has taken over.

properties.purpose: Coordinate broker membership and controller election, publish partition-leader metadata, and issue monotonically advancing fencing epochs. During a network partition, only the authoritative coordination quorum may elect a leader; a former leader must be rejected after failover. This control plane never carries stream records.

steps.phase: 3. Choose ordering, durability, and delivery semantics
steps.title: Use at-least-once delivery with idempotent effects
steps.content: Choose at-least-once delivery as the default across broker, processor, and sink boundaries. Stable event IDs and idempotent writes absorb retries. Claim exactly-once only inside a transaction boundary that atomically includes the relevant input offset, processor state, and output; an arbitrary external sink is not covered automatically.

decision.question: Which delivery guarantee should the default consumer path implement?
decision.chosen: At-least-once delivery with stable IDs, idempotent processing, and checkpoint-after-effect
decision.chosenReason: Retries and replay remain available after failures, while deduplication prevents repeated business effects. Exactly-once depends on a transaction spanning every state boundary involved.

alternatives.option: At-most-once with offset committed before processing
alternatives.tradeoff: Avoids duplicate processing but can permanently skip a record if the worker fails after advancing its offset.

alternatives.option: Exactly-once across broker and an arbitrary external sink
alternatives.tradeoff: The claim is invalid unless the sink participates in the same transaction or exposes an equivalent idempotent commit protocol.

properties.purpose: Continuously consume broker partitions for real-time filtering, transformation, joins, and stateful aggregation. Checkpoint operator state with input offsets, preserve partition order, and publish derived records through the broker. Use stable event IDs and idempotent effects for at-least-once retries; claim exactly-once only when input, state, and output share a supported transaction.

steps.phase: 3. Choose ordering, durability, and delivery semantics
steps.title: Replay from a group's committed offset
steps.content: Commit a consumer group's offset only after its effects are durable, or atomically with the effects when supported. Reset that group's cursor to an earlier retained offset to replay; keep other groups independent. Choose log retention from the required recovery and replay window because longer retention consumes more storage.

decision.question: How should replay progress be represented?
decision.chosen: A durable committed offset per consumer group and partition, advanced after effects
decision.chosenReason: Independent cursors allow a failed or new subscriber to reprocess retained records without moving another group's progress.

alternatives.option: One shared offset for all subscribers
alternatives.tradeoff: Uses less checkpoint metadata, but one group's progress can cause another group to skip records.

alternatives.option: Commit progress before the sink effect
alternatives.tradeoff: Simplifies retry behavior, but a crash between the offset commit and effect can lose the business result.

properties.purpose: Serve publish-subscribe streams from a partitioned append-only commit log. Route stable entity keys to partitions and preserve append order there. Replicate records across broker failure domains and acknowledge only after the selected in-sync replica commit policy is met. Store a durable offset per consumer group and partition; allow replay from earlier retained offsets, with retention chosen from product recovery needs.

steps.phase: 3. Choose ordering, durability, and delivery semantics
steps.title: Honor the 1 MB record limit without hiding latency cost
steps.content: Accept records up to the stated 1 MB limit and enforce the same maximum at clients and brokers. Batch only within a latency budget established from the real service objective; compression trades network and disk use for CPU. Do not silently convert large records into object references because that changes the record contract and replay dependency.

decision.question: How should the platform handle records up to 1 MB while keeping delivery latency low?
decision.chosen: Support the full 1 MB record in the stream path, validate size at both ends, and tune batching and compression from measured latency and workload
decision.chosenReason: The brief explicitly requires large records up to 1 MB and low-latency delivery. Measuring the workload exposes the network, storage, and CPU tradeoff without inventing a payload or latency target.

alternatives.option: Reject records below the stated maximum
alternatives.tradeoff: Can reduce resource use, but violates the explicit 1 MB support requirement.

alternatives.option: Store payloads externally and put references in the log
alternatives.tradeoff: Can reduce broker bytes, but adds a second durability, authorization, cleanup, and replay dependency not required by this brief.

properties.purpose: Publish records directly to the partition leader selected by broker metadata. Include a stable event ID for safe retries, choose a stable partition key where ordering matters, and support payloads up to the brief's 1 MB maximum with matching client and broker validation. Tune batching and compression against measured delivery latency and resource use.

steps.phase: 3. Choose ordering, durability, and delivery semantics
steps.title: Make workload assumptions explicit
steps.content: Assume each ordered record family has a stable partition key and each retried record has a stable event ID; if publishers cannot supply one, assign it at ingress. The brief does not specify traffic shape, partition count, replica count, failure-domain layout, latency objective, or replay-retention duration. Measure those inputs before selecting numeric settings.

steps.phase: 4. Scale from observed behavior and validate
steps.title: Scale broker partitions from measured load
steps.content: Use measured ingress rate, append latency, disk growth, and per-partition skew to decide whether more broker capacity or partitions are needed. A hot key remains serial within its partition; adding unrelated partitions does not remove that bottleneck.

scaleTrigger.metric: Measured publish rate, broker append latency, disk growth, and per-partition key skew
scaleTrigger.action: Benchmark the expected workload, then add broker capacity and partitions where observed parallelism or storage demand requires it; plan any key-remapping change explicitly.
scaleTrigger.impact: Increases horizontal capacity while retaining the per-partition ordering contract; an overloaded hot key may need a domain-level key redesign.

steps.phase: 4. Scale from observed behavior and validate
steps.title: Scale consumers from lag and partition parallelism
steps.content: Use lag age and growth, processing rate, checkpoint duration, and sink latency to locate the constrained stage. Add consumer members only up to useful partition parallelism, then scale the processor or sink that limits progress.

scaleTrigger.metric: Consumer lag by group and partition, processing throughput, checkpoint age, and sink latency
scaleTrigger.action: Add consumer capacity for independent assigned partitions and remove the measured bottleneck in the processor or sink; retain group offsets during reassignment.
scaleTrigger.impact: Improves catch-up and real-time processing without changing record order inside a partition or sharing offsets across groups.

steps.phase: 4. Scale from observed behavior and validate
steps.title: Exercise replica, coordinator, and consumer recovery
steps.content: Run failure exercises for broker loss, replica lag, coordinator quorum loss, processor restart, and sink timeout. Verify that only committed records survive, stale leaders are fenced, consumers resume from committed offsets, and duplicate delivery does not repeat sink effects.

scaleTrigger.metric: Under-replicated partitions, leader changes, coordinator quorum health, consumer lag, retries, and duplicate-effect checks
scaleTrigger.action: Inject each failure in a representative environment, verify the configured commit and fencing behavior, and tune replica placement or retry policy from observed recovery evidence.
scaleTrigger.impact: Demonstrates graceful recovery and exposes the availability cost of the selected durability and partition policy.

steps.phase: 4. Scale from observed behavior and validate
steps.title: Review the design against the brief
steps.content: The graph now has a publish path, replicated partition log, control-plane coordination, real-time processing, independent consumer groups, replayable offsets, an idempotent sink example, and operational signals. Validate the 1 MB path, ordering, acknowledged-write recovery, group replay, network-partition fencing, and measured throughput. No fixed partition count, replication factor, throughput threshold, latency target, or replay-retention duration is inferred from the brief.
